full_judgment: A. S. Faizul Islam Chowdhury J.— Civil Revision Nos. 1423 of 1970 and 811 of 1968 have been heard together, as similar question of law is involved in both the cases, and the same judgment is being delivered which shall govern both the revision cases. In Civil Revision No. 1423 of 1970 one Bacha Mia who is the petitioner was a railway guard under the Pakistan Eastern Railway and he was discharged from service by an order of the Chief traffic Manager, P.E. Railway on 21-4-53. Bacha Mia filed other Suit No. 146 of 1955 in the Court of the first Munsif, Chittagong Challenging the legality of the said order and the suit was dismissed. Then the petitioner preferred an appeal before the District Judge, who allowed the appeal on 16-6-59. The petitioner applied to the Railway Administration to allow him to resume his duties. After some correspondence the opposite party No. 2 directed Bacha Mia to join his post and by the same order the period of absence of Bacha Mia was ordered to be treated as leave with pay to the extent of the leave due, and the remaining period to be treated as leave without pay. After lengthy correspondence, Bacha Mia filed petition on 24-4-62 before the Authority (under Payment of Wages Act) under sub-section (2) of section 15 of the Payment of Wages Act for recovery of Rs. 12,686.75 being his delayed wages for the period from 21-4-53 to 31-1-62, and the same application was marked as Misc. Case No. 63 of 1962. The authority under the Payment of Wages Act who was the Munsif 1st Court, Chittagong. Sadar, dismissed the Misc. case, but the appeal to the District Judge against the decision of the Authority (Munsif) was allowed and the case was remanded back for disposal according to law; Then the opposite-parties filed a second appeal being Second Misc. Appeal No. 15 of 1965 before the High Court which was dismissed. Thereafter the Authority (Munsif) on receiving the case on remand allowed the Misc. case and then the appeal to the District Judge was allowed and the order passed by the Authority (Munsif) was set aside. So, the petitioner filed the present application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure before this Court and obtained the Rule.
